# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.

Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.

Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.

The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.

- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.

P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

## R15 OQ-52: confirmed option (a)
A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

## R16 OQ-DO-30: option (A)
The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

## R17 Interaction OQ 48: confirmed
A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

## R18 Player Controller OQ 29(ii): pre-ruled conditional
If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

## R19 Boarding OQ-BS-34 fallback: pre-ruled conditional
If the boarding spike finds no K3 pass line inside 21-28 tiles with Attention's levers, the X3 route band's upper end widens to 31 tiles for the reference sortie (lower end stays 21). Not applied now; the spike decides.

Every item marked "Default applied ... pending user confirmation" or "(confirm)" in any GDD is confirmed as of 2026-10-28 by delegation. Re-mark it "confirmed 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R20" and remove it from open user-decision lists. Do not change the value.

Any other "USER DECISION" left in a GDD is decided by its creative-director lean (G2) or, absent one, by the option that preserves prior user rulings and needs the least new content; record it as delegated ruling R21 with one sentence of reason. Never leave a "USER DECISION" open.

905	**Output Range:** with the defaults `interval_ticks` = 5 * 4 = **20 ticks (3 per second) at every gait**: `STRIDE_WALK` 10 at `V_WALK` 2, `STRIDE_RUN` 15 at `V_RUN` 3 and `STRIDE_CARRY` 5 at `V_CARRY` 1 each advance one animation frame per 5 ticks. **Gait changes the level and the timbre, never the rate:** the run is -3 dBr, the walk and the carry -9 dBr (carry footfall is flat and never scales with carried mass, `IDB:991`). A slowed avatar steps proportionally slower, and a time-stepped state (stagger, work, idle, down: PC-11 steps them at 12 fps from committed tick counts, not from the odometer) fires **no** footfall, the Suit's stagger gasp being the sound of a stagger; a diagonal keeps the cadence because the odometer weights each axis. The footstep is never a function of `level_pm`, locus distance, `phase`, Horror state or sanity.
906	**Example:** run 120 ticks (2 s): the odometer advances 360 px, which is 24 frames, three 8-frame cycles, so 6 footfalls at -3 dBr. Walk 120 ticks: 240 px, 24 frames, 6 footfalls at -9 dBr. Carry 120 ticks: 120 px, 24 frames, 6 footfalls at -9 dBr. Over 40 ticks each gait produces exactly 2. An avatar pressed into a wall for 120 ticks: the odometer is unchanged, 0 footfalls. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Back-pedal: walking east while facing west for 40 ticks advances the odometer by 80 px = 8 frames but `dir` = -1, so `anim_counter_a` falls by 8 and the frame passes through the contact frames in reverse; exactly 2 footfalls, at the same cadence as a forward walk (the cadence follows the animated foot, not the direction). Stop-start: a walk that stops with `frame` = 4 and resumes 30 ticks later fires nothing at the resume and the next footfall at the next contact frame.

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

905	**Output Range:** with the defaults `interval_ticks` = 5 * 4 = **20 ticks (3 per second) at every gait**: `STRIDE_WALK` 10 at `V_WALK` 2, `STRIDE_RUN` 15 at `V_RUN` 3 and `STRIDE_CARRY` 5 at `V_CARRY` 1 each advance one animation frame per 5 ticks. **Gait changes the level and the timbre, never the rate:** the run is -3 dBr, the walk and the carry -9 dBr (carry footfall is flat and never scales with carried mass, `IDB:991`). A slowed avatar steps proportionally slower, and a time-stepped state (stagger, work, idle, down: PC-11 steps them at 12 fps from committed tick counts, not from the odometer) fires **no** footfall, the Suit's stagger gasp being the sound of a stagger; a diagonal keeps the cadence because the odometer weights each axis. content.content:
**Level contract: a quiet, slow breath, never a constant tone** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R8)*. SOUND stays **independent of visibility** (not gated on on-screen or lit): Audio owns distance attenuation, so an off-screen lie attenuates naturally; each leak mode must be sufficient alone (HR-5), which a visibility-gated sound would break for exactly the player who looks away; and the location-oracle risk (a sound that says "something over there lies") is accepted because it points at a surface to doubt, never at the truth, and Audio's attenuation bounds it (the review ruled against gating on on-screen and lit). The request contract *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R8)* (the Filter is the producer of the request, so it defines the unit and Audio converts, ruling R8; the 2026-10-27 design-review text that scaled LEVEL against a "quietest consequence-channel class" reference Audio does not define is withdrawn): (1) **unit**: `LEVEL(pm)`, and the level an ON carries, is `amp_snd`, an integer per mille of `AMP_MAX_PM` (0 to 1000), the lie's discrepancy envelope of D.5 with the gleam's own breath factor removed; it is the value Adaptive Audio D.15 receives as `leak_amplitude_pm` (0 to 1000) and maps linearly onto `HAL_FLOOR_DB` to `HAL_CEIL_DB`. **AA-35. The `hal` family, its MVP signature and its audio leak (the "violet of sound").**
*Rule.* `hal` ids are the Filter's `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES` namespace, cited by reference (PF-20): MVP `FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` (needle, readout, card, glyph) and `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` (housing, machine); VS-A `FA_PHANTOM_MOVE` and `FA_PHANTOM_PRESENCE`. **At MVP there is one sound signature, the class-(b) reading-lie signature, realised under two Filter ids by surface type**; the two ids share the reserved signature and differ only in surface-appropriate content (a quiet sound under a needle versus under a lamp housing or machine), and the family is lint-disjoint from every other family (AA-6). *(Ruling R1 wrote "exactly one class"; PF-20 publishes two MVP ids; both are one class-(b) signature, and the wording tension is resolved at the 2026-10-26 checkpoint: CX-F2 and OQ-AA-10 are closed.)* Every `hal` sound is recognisable by a **reserved signature no other family may use**: (i) a detuned fringe partial in a reserved band; (ii) a slow amplitude breathing at the same period as the violet fringe (4 to 6 s per cycle, `ART:563`; cited, not restated); (iii) a tail that over-reaches its source. Mood "doubt, not horror" (`SN:1259-1262`): wrong, warm, fringed; no heartbeat, no tempo change, no sting; the class-(c) victim fringe is silent. The reserved band is an asset-spec and import-tag constraint enforced by the identity-table lint (AA-6 f, AA-45); this GDD states the **perceptual property and the test**, not a filter chain: blind two-clip identification of the lying instrument by sound alone at or above 90 per cent, **a near-field distinctness test** (the AC-SE-42 analogue; the tester stands already within the instrument's reading range, `HAL_RADIUS_PX` and AA-36, so it measures whether the signature is distinct, never whether a lie can be detected from afar) and, with hue removed and with audio removed in turn, a trained tester still identifies the lying instrument above chance (HR-5). The first lie carries all three leak modes (violet gleam, glide, sound); the Filter may drop only the SOUND mode, at stage 2 or 3, never on the first lie; GLEAM and the motion mode are mandatory on every lie (SN-15 L-L; PF-15), and a lie whose SOUND mode is dropped has **no audio request at all**. At MVP `MODE_DROP_PM` is 0, so every MVP lie has a sound.
*Why.* R-6 (`ART:962`): if audio can lie it needs a leak equivalent to violet. A pitch detune alone is confusable with a real groaning pump (P1); a glitch artefact reads as "audio glitch" (`ART:851`), the "scanline for the lie".
*Pillar.* P4, P1. *Decided by.* run ruling R2; HR-5; SN-25; `SN:256`; PF-20.

**AA-36. `hal` transport and states `(designed; re-checked at the X-6 scan)`.**
*Rule.* Audio never reads `sanity.perception` (SN-23, CR-12). It consumes only what the Filter supplies, per local viewer: the request `(viewer, ref or position, intent in {ON, LEVEL(pm), OFF}, class)` of PF-20 and, for a lying instrument, the `leak_modes` of the Filter's `perceived(ref, viewer)` pull (PF-8). **ON** is requested on the first ACTIVE frame, so the sound begins **no later than the glide** (`t_sound_on <= t_glide_visible`, SN:1256, PF-15: "the sound request is emitted on the first ACTIVE frame, not when the needle has visibly moved"); **LEVEL** follows `leak_amplitude_pm` (D.15); **OFF** arrives at CLEAR, and after an entry leaves `sanity.perception` the level follows the remaining discrepancy, then off, **presentation-identical for expired, debunked and invalidated lies with no verdict flash and no relief cue** (PF-12). The audible start of the leak is within `SOUND_LEAD_MAX_MS` (Filter, 100 ms `[PLACEHOLDER]`, PF D.15) of the first ACTIVE frame. The measured device latency is part of spike AC-AA-6 and OQ-AA-4. LEVEL arrives quantised by `AUDIO_LEVEL_STEP_PM` (Filter, 20); Audio slews between received levels at the constant `RUN_SLEW_DB_PER_TICK` of D.7 (`RUN_SLEW_REF_DB / RUN_SLEW_TICKS` = 0.2 dB per tick, the one slew rate of the mix; no separate `hal` slew knob exists) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the rate is now defined in dB per tick, so it is the same whatever the ceiling and floor are)* and never extrapolates. Where the whole transport lies (a `PERCEPTION_OUT` request view versus the pull query) is the Filter's to fix; this GDD states only the fields it needs and renders neither a sound for a remote viewer (the Filter returns the honest record for any remote PlayerId, PF-10) nor a sound when the SOUND mode is not in force. A ref that resolves to a world surface is positional at that surface; a ref that resolves to a card or HUD reading is non-positional in the viewer's own space `(provisional — HUD and Instruments undesigned)`. Requests are `OWNER_PRIVATE` per seat. **Audible radius (`HAL_RADIUS_PX`, P4 verification economy).** The `hal` leak of a world-surface ref is audible only within `R_hal(ref) = min(HAL_RADIUS_PX, legibility_range_px(ref))` of the viewer's avatar, where `legibility_range_px(ref)` is the range at which the lying instrument's sprite is legible, so the leak can **never be heard from farther away than the instrument can be read**: spotting a lie by ear then costs the same approach (time and risk) as reading it, and checking is never free (P4: "checking costs time, risk or trust"). Beyond `R_hal` the `hal` voice is not requested from the pool (a cull, not a duck), fading in and out over `HAL_FADE_TICKS` at the boundary, with no sting. Only the `hal` voice is bounded: the instrument's true running or witness sound (AA-24, AA-26) is a different family, is untouched by this radius and keeps its own audible floor (AA-11, AA-25), so a lying gauge over a stalling pump still has the pump heard beyond `R_hal` (the falsifier, AA-37 e). A ref that resolves to a card or HUD reading is already non-positional and in the viewer's own space; it has no distance and `HAL_RADIUS_PX` does not apply to it. `legibility_range_px(ref)` is a read-only datum owned by the render and instrument layer `(provisional — Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: In-World Instruments is now designed and cites the datum (`IW:1398`, "never above `legibility_range_px` of the lying surface") without defining or registering it; the ask to publish and register `legibility_range_px(ref)` is routed (OQ-AA-39). Until it is published the rule is R_hal = HAL_RADIUS_PX, with HAL_RADIUS_PX held at the placeholder bound in Tuning Knobs §H as the fallback; once the datum exists, a HAL_RADIUS_PX above a surface's legibility range is applied as the min() and logged once as a DIAGNOSTIC, not refused (E-AA-60))`. If the Filter refuses to emit audio requests, MVP class-(b) lies play **no** reading-lie sound and HR-5's sound mode is unmet. **Disposition (creative-director, CD-GDD-ALIGN):** the Filter must emit audio requests for every MVP class-(b) lie while `MODE_DROP_PM` is 0; a refusal reopens PF-20, not AA-35. Audio does not design around it: it keeps no reading-lie sound and the CONFLICT diagnostic (E-AA-51, AC-AA-60).
*Pillar.* P4. *Decided by.* run ruling R3; PF-20, PF-12, PF-15, PF-10; SN-23.

| State | Entry (Filter request) | Audio action | Exit | Who causes it |

| restore | the post-restore notification | resume in whatever state the Filter reports from the first frame (no clean frame) | as above | Save/Load, the Filter |

input.notes: One BLOCKING item (the hal-leak contract), one root cause: the Filter (publisher; registry source of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM) sends LEVEL = unbreathed amp_snd and an ON payload (LEVEL, T_s 4000-6000 ms, floor 500), while Audio D.15 reads perceived().leak_amplitude_pm (the breathed gleam amplitude, PF-8) and breathes again with its own 400/300 constants. Classified CONFLICT (G1/R8: Audio conforms) with an INTERNAL recompute (G4). D.15 now takes LEVEL and (T_s, floor), converts T_s at 60 ticks/s (5473 ms -> 328 ticks), applies the breath once, and keeps HAL_BREATH_* as fallbacks only, with a guard for invalid payloads (T_s = 0, out-of-range floor). R-j recomputed: at the old HAL_FLOOR_DB -33 with the Filter's 0.5 trough it is -33 - 6.02 - 4.5 = -43.52 against -42.23, 1.29 dB short. The least invasive fix is HAL_FLOOR_DB -33 -> -31 (minimum -31.71 at floor 500), giving -41.52 with 0.71 dB spare. HAL_RADIUS_PX stays at 192 so AC-AA-129 and the P4 verification economy are untouched, and R-a, R-c to R-e, R-h and R-i are unchanged because they bind HAL_CEIL_DB. The coupling is recorded: R-j holds only for SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM >= 461 (fallback depth <= 539). The Filter's registered range 300-800 is not changed, because the Filter owns it. Cascade: AC-AA-57 is rewritten (the old depth-850 refusal vector no longer refuses; use 900 or a floor of 100), AC-AA-134's R-j spare goes 0.29 -> 0.71, AC-AA-108 and the new AC-AA-157 and AC-AA-158 cover the single modulation, the fallback and the guards, and AAV-34, F5, OQ-AA-22 and AA-35 (ii) drop the 'same period / derive phase from the lie-time' pairing. Sibling Filter fixes: its worked conversion still quotes Audio's stale -42/24 dB defaults, and it says Audio reads the sound level as leak_amplitude_pm although PF-8 defines that field as the breathed gleam amplitude. No other GDD quotes these numbers (Sanity's AA-35 cites are only 'can audio lie'). The StructuredOutput target enum has no registry option, so the registry changes are routed through Audio's X-5 convention and need the orchestrator: update the entities.yaml hal_level formula (about L5747-5750) to LEVEL_pm, the (T_s, floor) envelope and HAL_FLOOR_DB -31, and add adaptive-audio-and-tells.md to referenced_by of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM. Deliberately not planned: the Filter's 'combined cap' sub-ask in OQ-PF-39, which is separate from this blocker and stays open, and the CD's deaf-player accessibility item, which is not a blocker. Every edit should carry the *(Amended 2026-10-28 ...)* marker, and G3 greps are listed in the X-5 request.

toolu_01DtLzMWSeGyvaPSgbCTYryR.notes: One BLOCKING item (the hal-leak contract), one root cause: the Filter (publisher; registry source of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM) sends LEVEL = unbreathed amp_snd and an ON payload (LEVEL, T_s 4000-6000 ms, floor 500), while Audio D.15 reads perceived().leak_amplitude_pm (the breathed gleam amplitude, PF-8) and breathes again with its own 400/300 constants. D.15 now takes LEVEL and (T_s, floor), converts T_s at 60 ticks/s (5473 ms -> 328 ticks), applies the breath once, and keeps HAL_BREATH_* as fallbacks only, with a guard for invalid payloads (T_s = 0, out-of-range floor). R-j recomputed: at the old HAL_FLOOR_DB -33 with the Filter's 0.5 trough it is -33 - 6.02 - 4.5 = -43.52 against -42.23, 1.29 dB short. No other GDD quotes these numbers (Sanity's AA-35 cites are only 'can audio lie'). The StructuredOutput target enum has no registry option, so the registry changes are routed through Audio's X-5 convention and need the orchestrator: update the entities.yaml hal_level formula (about L5747-5750) to LEVEL_pm, the (T_s, floor) envelope and HAL_FLOOR_DB -31, and add adaptive-audio-and-tells.md to referenced_by of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM. data.notes: One BLOCKING item (the hal-leak contract), one root cause: the Filter (publisher; registry source of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM) sends LEVEL = unbreathed amp_snd and an ON payload (LEVEL, T_s 4000-6000 ms, floor 500), while Audio D.15 reads perceived().leak_amplitude_pm (the breathed gleam amplitude, PF-8) and breathes again with its own 400/300 constants. Classified CONFLICT (G1/R8: Audio conforms) with an INTERNAL recompute (G4). D.15 now takes LEVEL and (T_s, floor), converts T_s at 60 ticks/s (5473 ms -> 328 ticks), applies the breath once, and keeps HAL_BREATH_* as fallbacks only, with a guard for invalid payloads (T_s = 0, out-of-range floor). R-j recomputed: at the old HAL_FLOOR_DB -33 with the Filter's 0.5 trough it is -33 - 6.02 - 4.5 = -43.52 against -42.23, 1.29 dB short. The least invasive fix is HAL_FLOOR_DB -33 -> -31 (minimum -31.71 at floor 500), giving -41.52 with 0.71 dB spare. HAL_RADIUS_PX stays at 192 so AC-AA-129 and the P4 verification economy are untouched, and R-a, R-c to R-e, R-h and R-i are unchanged because they bind HAL_CEIL_DB. The coupling is recorded: R-j holds only for SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM >= 461 (fallback depth <= 539). The Filter's registered range 300-800 is not changed, because the Filter owns it. Cascade: AC-AA-57 is rewritten (the old depth-850 refusal vector no longer refuses; use 900 or a floor of 100), AC-AA-134's R-j spare goes 0.29 -> 0.71, AC-AA-108 and the new AC-AA-157 and AC-AA-158 cover the single modulation, the fallback and the guards, and AAV-34, F5, OQ-AA-22 and AA-35 (ii) drop the 'same period / derive phase from the lie-time' pairing. No other GDD quotes these numbers (Sanity's AA-35 cites are only 'can audio lie'). The StructuredOutput target enum has no registry option, so the registry changes are routed through Audio's X-5 convention and need the orchestrator: update the entities.yaml hal_level formula (about L5747-5750) to LEVEL_pm, the (T_s, floor) envelope and HAL_FLOOR_DB -31, and add adaptive-audio-and-tells.md to referenced_by of SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM.
